title: Engineering materials: strong, stiff and tough
examples: Teacher, can you show us an example of a material that is very tough?
What makes steel different from regular iron?
If something is stiff, does that mean it is also strong?

explain.say: Today we are looking at how materials are tested.

draw.text: Engineering materials: strong, stiff and tough

explain.say: Strength is how much force a material can take before breaking.
Stiffness measures how much a material resists bending when pushed.
Toughness is the ability to absorb energy before it breaks apart.
Steel is very strong and quite stiff, making it useful for buildings.
Concrete is excellent at resisting compression forces, which is why it is used in foundations.

faq.q: What is the main difference between strength and toughness?
faq.a: Strength is about the maximum force before failure. Toughness is about how much energy the material can soak up before it fails.
asks: Can you explain the difference between these two?

faq.q: Are composites always stronger than pure metals?
faq.a: Composites combine different materials for better overall properties. They are designed to be better than their individual parts.
asks: What makes a composite material better?
Do I need two materials to make a composite?

faq.q: Why do we use concrete instead of just steel for buildings?
faq.a: Concrete is very strong when squeezed, which is called compression. Steel is better at being pulled apart.
asks: Which material is better for foundations?
Can concrete hold up a roof?

faq.q: Does 'stiff' mean the same thing as 'strong'?
faq.a: No, stiffness means resisting bending, while strength means resisting breaking under tension or compression.
asks: If it bends a lot, is it weak?
What does it mean to resist bending?

faq.a: Composites are made by combining two or more different materials together. Examples include fiberglass or carbon fibre.
asks: Can I mix materials to make something new?
What is the basic idea of a composite?

facts: Steel is an alloy of iron and carbon, making it very strong.
Concrete gains its strength from the chemical reaction between cement and water.
Composites combine materials like fibres and a matrix to improve properties.
Toughness is measured by the area under a stress-strain curve.

quiz.say: A material that can withstand a very large impact without shattering is showing which property?
quiz.why: Toughness specifically measures the ability to absorb energy from a sudden impact.

wrong.0: Strength only measures the maximum force before breaking, not the energy absorbed.
wrong.1: Stiffness describes resistance to bending, which is different from impact resistance.
wrong.2: Ductility is about being able to stretch into a wire, not necessarily absorbing impact energy.

quiz.say: If you are designing a bridge support that must resist bending from wind, which property is most important?
quiz.why: Stiffness directly relates to how much the material will bend or deflect under a given load.

wrong.0: Strength is important, but a very strong material can still bend too much if it lacks stiffness.
wrong.1: Toughness is about sudden shocks, while wind loading is a continuous bending force.
wrong.2: Hardness measures resistance to scratching, which is not the main concern for wind load.

quiz.say: A material that is very hard to scratch but breaks easily when hit is low in which property?
quiz.why: The description points to low energy absorption upon impact, which is the definition of low toughness.

wrong.0: Elasticity describes returning to shape, but the problem focuses on failure upon impact.
wrong.2: It might have high strength, but the key failure mode described is impact, not simple breaking.
wrong.3: The problem describes failure upon impact, not excessive bending under load.
